findings.message: The new guard prevents voluntary context switches, allowing tasks with preemption disabled to continue executing after blocking calls. On SMP with configUSE_TASK_PREEMPTION_DISABLE=1, call vTaskPreemptionDisable(NULL) followed by vTaskDelay(10). vTaskDelay calls prvAddCurrentTaskToDelayedList(), which removes the caller from the ready list, then requests a yield. The new vTaskSwitchContext branch only sets xYieldPendings and skips task selection, so the same task resumes and vTaskDelay returns while its TCB remains on the delayed list.

Requiring a false-to-true transition of the pending-yield flag can suppress an ISR wake flag and delay a higher-priority task until a later tick. With preemption enabled on SMP, an ISR can notify a blocked task using a NULL wake-flag pointer, setting the calling core's xYieldPendings without requesting a hardware switch. If another notification then unblocks a higher-priority task pinned to that core with a fresh wake flag, xYieldPendingBefore is already true, so the new condition leaves the flag false. prvYieldForTask skips cores with a pending yield, and vTaskExitCriticalFromISR does not issue one. The same transition check also affects xTaskResumeFromISR, xTaskRemoveFromEventList and vTaskGenericNotifyGiveFromISR.
